def: Learning the quirks and noise of the training examples so that performance on new data is worse than on the training set.
Any change to a learning procedure that gives up a little training accuracy in return for better accuracy on unseen data.
Adding a penalty proportional to the squared size of the weights to the loss, which pulls every weight towards zero.
Multiplying the weights by a factor slightly below one at every step, so that only weights the data keeps pushing stay large.
Adam with weight decay applied outside the adaptive update, so that the decay strength does not depend on gradient size.
Zeroing a random subset of hidden units at each training step so that no unit can depend on particular partners.
Dropout in which the surviving units are scaled by 1/(1 - p) during training, so that no change is needed at evaluation time.
Creating extra training examples by applying transformations that are known not to change the label.
Ending training when held-out loss stops improving and restoring the weights from the best evaluation.
The number of evaluations without improvement that early stopping tolerates before it ends the run.
The model size at which a model can just barely fit its training data exactly, where test error often peaks.
The pattern in which test error falls, spikes near the interpolation threshold, and falls again as the model keeps growing.
